answer: An agent economy can make high-impact actions conditional on a bond locked in a public contract: each identity stakes funds, and a randomly selected set of established agents reviews its work. If an agent submits provably false claims, reviewers can slash its bond; honest agents are rewarded for detecting fraud. This does not make identities scarce by itself, but it makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must fund many bonds and risks losing them. A sonnet, a bridge, or a ridge of copied profiles gains no weight without stake.
